doc.title: Ashley Keating and Allan Whitworth Interview, 1963-03-22

chapter: Early life and the Brisbane band
title: Opinion of New Orleans musicians' dedication
summary: Asked about the local musicians, Keating gives a first impression that they play the music naturally but make concessions to big crowds.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Ha, ha, ha, ha, ha, ha, ha. What do you think about the musicians here? Do you consider themselves... Do you think they consider themselves fanatics or do you think they're constantly making compromises or...?
Uh, uh, uh... From what I've seen...
That's why we're on the set.

From what I've seen, I...I wouldn't really term too many of them dedicated. I'd say this is just an on-the-spot review. I may live to regret this, but I'd say the Negro ones, which are the only ones I've really heard since I've been here, seem to play this way because they know no other way. But if there's a big crowd, they appear to me to certainly make concessions towards them. Perhaps it's through years of scuffling and hard going that they think they have to. Personally, I don't think they do. I think they'd get the people in, whether they played Gettysburg March instead of Bill Bailey or not.
